successors.name: Roman Republic
successors.text: 'between the Loire (Liger) and the Saône (Arar) (modern Burgundy)': Loire on the west against the Bituriges, Saône on the east against the Sequani; Bibracte on Mont Beuvray

ledger.x: c. 150 BC: the Aedui, Rome's first inner-Gaulish allies. 'The alliance was concluded around 150-140 BC' (undated) and they were allies 'from the middle of the 2nd century BC'; a foedus aequum, and 'fratres populi Romani' in Tacitus. The page gives no founding of the tribe; 150 is the first date the page offers (page…
The Aedui lead a clientele: 'The Segusiavi were clients to the south, and the Mandubii to the north.'
52 BC: the Aedui join the revolt.
52 BC: the Aeduan clientele ends with the revolt (the Mandubii hold Alesia against Caesar).
September 52 BC: Alesia ends the revolt.
September 52 BC: the Aedui come under Rome again.
September 52 BC: the independent Aedui end; the civitas lives on as an ally of Rome with Bibracte, then Augustodunum, as its centre.

wars.name: Gallic Wars: Caesar's intervention against Ariovistus (58 BC)
wars.outcome: Caesar intervened 'at the Aedui's request' against the Germani of Ariovistus, allied with the Sequani; Diviciacus guided the legions into Alsace.

wars.name: Revolt of Vercingetorix (Gallic Wars, 52 BC)
wars.outcome: The Aedui joined the revolt briefly; Alesia (September 52) ended organised resistance and the Aedui kept their laws and title.

certainty.note: The Loire and the Saone are the only limits given; the eastern boundary with the Sequani was irregular.
